items.title: Kyiv Faces Russian Missile Barrage, Naftogaz Facilities Damaged
items.author: Olesia Safronova
items.content: <article>Ukraine’s capital and the region surrounding Kyiv faced another Russian missile barrage overnight targeting energy facilities and bridges, with at least one civilian killed and several injured.</article>

items.title: Czech Premier Blasts Central Bank Rate Hike as ‘Scandalous’
items.author: Michal Kubala
items.content: <article>Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babis stepped up his public criticism of the country’s central bank following this week’s interest-rate hike, calling the board’s decision “absolutely scandalous” and saying it will hurt households and companies.</article>

items.title: Finland Considers Ukraine-Style Tank Barriers as Russia Rearms
items.author: Kirsi Heikel
items.content: In Ukraine, anti-tank obstacles have slowed the attacker. Now Finland wants to see how such structures would fare in harsh northern weather.

items.title: New Zealand Election Kingmaker Emerges With 50% of Vote Counted
items.author: Ainsley Thomson and Tracy Withers
items.content: <article>New Zealand’s two main parties are neck-and-neck with half the votes counted in the nation’s election, but projections currently show both political blocs are may need the support of the centrist Opportunity Party, which is on track to enter parliament for the first time.</article>

items.title: Burnham Bets That Britain Can Move Past the Old Brexit Divisions
items.author: Chloe Chaplain and Alex Wickham
items.content: <article>In British politics, dividing lines have formed around Brexit for the past decade, often replacing traditional right-and-left allegiances. Now, Andy Burnham is backing himself to redraw the political map all over again.</article>

items.title: Malaysian King Says No Ambiguity on Najib’s Home Detention Order
items.author: Liau Y-Sing
items.content: <article>Malaysia’s king declared there was no ambiguity over his pardon for former Prime Minister Najib Razak, warning that any challenge to the decree amounts to defying his authority as the attorney general’s office calls for a delay in its implementation.</article>

items.title: Hong Kong Arrests 28 in Building Bid-Rigging Probe, RTHK Says
items.author: Aileen Chuang
items.content: <article>Hong Kong authorities arrested 28 people tied to a suspected triad-linked bid-rigging syndicate targeting building maintenance and renovation contracts, Radio Television Hong Kong reported, citing Secretary for Security Chris Tang.</article>

items.title: US Believes Woman Close to Nvidia CEO Was a China Spy, NYT Says
items.author: John Harney
items.content: <article>US intelligence officials told the Trump administration that a woman who had become close to Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang was working for a Chinese spy agency, which recruited her to collect information on him, the New York Times reported Friday.</article>

items.title: Australia’s Albanese Urges Iran De-Escalation After US Midterms
items.author: Richard Henderson
items.content: <article>Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has called for a de-escalation of tensions between the US and Iran after the midterm elections, which he described as “very significant,” according to a report from the Australian Broadcasting Corp.</article>

items.title: Wall Street Week | Blue Wave Economic Impacts, European Welfare Woes
items.content: <article>This week, Columbia Business School professor Glenn Hubbard breaks down the economic implications of the US midterm elections. Meanwhile, rising oil prices are both a burden and a benefit in Alaska. And, we go into the field with Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin to get a closer look at American manufacturing. Plus, Europe’s postwar welfare programs are facing new challenges amid budget crunches and growing youth protests. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Trump Touts Plan for US Air Show, Seeks to Turn Page on Midterm
items.author: Kate Sullivan
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump sought to shrug off his Republican Party’s disastrous midterm defeat during a visit to Florida, touting plans to launch a new US air show as an example of how his economic agenda is revitalizing American industry.</article>

items.title: Wiles Out as White House Chief of Staff, Stephen Miller Takes Role
items.content: <article>"Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Joe Manchin, former US Senator and Governor for West Virginia, says Democrats can overplay their hand if they make impeaching President Donald Trump a priority after taking control of Congress. Rep. Don Beyer (D-VA) says he was thrilled that a federal judge temporarily blocked President Donald Trump's planned triumphal arch from breaking ground. Rep. Gwen Moore (D-WI) says affordability is “top of mind for all Americans” and believes health care is an obvious place for Democrats to intervene. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Coinbase’s Ryan VanGrack Says Crypto Clarity Is Advancing
items.content: <article>Coinbase Vice Chair Ryan VanGrack says legislation has stalled since the Clarity Act vote, but the SEC and CFTC are advancing regulatory measures that are providing another route to clarity. He added that crypto is inherently bipartisan, even as regulatory proposals may face congressional scrutiny and debate. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: Chip Stocks Rebound
items.content:
<article>The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF

A rebound in chipmakers propped up the stock market as dip buyers emerged despite economic data that reinforced speculation the Federal Reserve will boost rates in December. Technology stocks staged a sharp recovery, but whether that holds is another matter. Meantime, President Trump said he was tapping longtime aide Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff and that Susie Wiles will move to his political operation, shaking up his White House team days after a devastating midterm result. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Bremmer: U.S. Retreat From Global Leadership Is a Long-Term Shift
items.content: <article>Ian Bremmer says Tuesday’s election should be viewed against structural changes in U.S. policy that are likely to persist regardless of which party holds the White House. He cites weaker support for free-trade agreements and a greater reliance on industrial policy, subsidies and tariffs. Bremmer speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Affordability First, Open to Hegseth Impeachment: Rep. Moore
items.content: <article>Rep. Gwen Moore (D-WI) says affordability is “top of mind for all Americans” and believes health care is an obvious place for Democrats to intervene. Rep. Moore says Democrats' agenda should not be “first and foremost” to impeach people, but says she will not push for impeachment of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and that it would be “hard not to vote yes” on Rep. Thomas Massie's privileged resolution. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Rep. Beyer: Democrats Were Not Elected to Impeach Trump
items.content: <article>Rep. Don Beyer (D-VA) says he was thrilled that a federal judge temporarily blocked President Donald Trump's planned triumphal arch from breaking ground. Rep. Beyer says he is depending on the courts and public sentiment to stop the project and has legislation aimed at preventing it from moving forward. Rep. Beyer says Democrats were not elected to impeach President Trump, but to stop the war and bring health care back to Americans. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Manchin: Democrats Risk Overplaying Hand on Impeachment
items.content: <article>Joe Manchin, former US Senator and Governor for West Virginia, says Democrats can overplay their hand if they make impeaching President Donald Trump a priority after taking control of Congress. Manchin says Democrats should instead pass legislation addressing tariffs and public officials profiting from their positions and “try everything possible to put the genie back in the bottle.” Manchin says Trump will have to work with Congress because executive orders “only go so far and only last so long.” He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Paraguayan President Peña Removed From Office, Arrested
items.author: Ken Parks
items.content: <article>Paraguay’s Senate removed President Santiago Peña from office Friday, a dramatic downfall that paves the way for him to face potential criminal charges over his alleged role in the collapse of a major bank.</article>

items.title: Trump Taps Stephen Miller to Replace Wiles as Chief of Staff
items.author: Jeff Mason and Courtney Subramanian
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump said he was tapping longtime aide Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff and that Susie Wiles is moving to his political operation, shaking up his White House team days after a devastating midterm result.</article>
